prompt: A service needs two busy vCPUs and settles at 12 GiB of memory. On the price sheet, which E2 choice wastes least while staying predefined?
hint: Lesson 1. Pick the ratio before the size.

choices.text: e2-standard-4, 4 vCPU and 16 GiB, at 97.84 a month
choices.why: It carries two vCPUs nobody uses, for 31.85 more a month.

choices.text: e2-standard-2, 2 vCPU and 8 GiB, at 48.92
choices.why: 8 GiB is less than the 12 the service settles at.

choices.text: e2-highmem-2, 2 vCPU and 16 GiB, at 65.99
choices.why: Right. The ratio fits, with 4 GiB of headroom.

choices.text: e2-medium, sharing a core, at 24.46
choices.why: 4 GiB and one vCPU of share: far below the need.

prompt: With N4 custom rates of 0.03275 per vCPU-hour and 0.003717 per GiB-hour, what does n4-custom-4-20480 cost for a month of 730 hours, in USD?
hint: Lesson 1. 20480 MiB is 20 GiB.

prompt: terraform plan accepted a machine_type nobody offers and planned "1 to add". Which part of Google checks the name, and when?
hint: Lesson 1. The catalogue lives zone by zone.

choices.text: Compute Engine, on the API call that creates the machine
choices.why: Right. A clean plan says the file is coherent, not that Google would accept it.

choices.text: The provider, when terraform init installs it
choices.why: The provider checks the file's shape and knows no catalogue.

choices.text: gcloud, the next time its configuration is listed
choices.why: gcloud config list shows settings, not machine types.

choices.text: Cloud Billing, when the first invoice is drawn up
choices.why: Billing never sees a machine that was not created.

prompt: A team runs a web server that is busy every afternoon on e2-small to save money, and users complain of slowness at exactly those hours. What is the most likely cause?
hint: Lesson 1. What does a shared core guarantee?

choices.text: Spot preemption every afternoon
choices.why: Nothing here is Spot, and preemption stops a machine rather than slowing it.

choices.text: A sustained use discount that throttles busy machines
choices.why: Discounts change the bill, never the speed; and E2 gets none.

choices.text: Extended memory charged at a higher rate
choices.why: e2-small has 2 GiB; extended memory is a custom-type feature.

choices.text: A steady load held to half a vCPU once the burst is spent
choices.why: Right. A burst covers short peaks, never an afternoon.

prompt: Google's monthly figures, and this course's, count a month as ___ hours.
hint: Lesson 1. 8,760 over twelve.

prompt: A webhook receives one request every two seconds, each of 100 ms, all day. Which Cloud Run billing mode should it use, by lesson 22's arithmetic?
hint: Lesson 22. Busy fraction: 1 - e^(-0.5 × 0.1).

choices.text: Instance-based: the traffic arrives every hour of the day
choices.why: Arriving all day is not being busy; the instance is empty 95% of the time.

choices.text: Request-based: the instance is busy about 5% of the time
choices.why: Right. Far below the 75% line where instance-based starts to win.

choices.text: Either: below 2 million requests both are free
choices.why: The free requests belong to request-based billing only.

choices.text: Instance-based, with a minimum of one instance
choices.why: That pays all day for an instance that is busy 5% of it.

prompt: Cloud Run charges 0.40 USD per million requests under request-based billing. Ignoring the free tier, what is the fee on 300 million requests a month?
hint: Lesson 22.

prompt: Why does lesson 22 rule out options by their limits before pricing them?
hint: Lesson 22. A cheaper option that cannot carry the work.

choices.text: Because pricing is slow and limits are quick to read
choices.why: Speed of work is not the argument.

choices.text: Because Google refuses to quote prices for unsupported workloads
choices.why: Price pages are public for every service.

choices.text: Because an option that cannot carry the workload is not an option at any price
choices.why: Right. Ten minutes of checking saves the meeting after the migration started.

choices.text: Because limits are the same on every provider
choices.why: They differ, which is exactly why they decide.

prompt: Order these by their monthly cost for the busy profile in lesson 22, cheapest first.
hint: Lesson 22. 400 requests a second around the clock.
trap: Request-based billing is last because of its fee on about a billion requests, not because of its rate.

prompt: A service keeps uploaded files in /tmp. Which move costs it least work?
hint: Lesson 22. Which option keeps local state by accident?

choices.text: To a single Compute Engine machine
choices.why: Right. Nothing changes, at the price of a machine that can fail with the files on it.

choices.text: To Cloud Run with several instances
choices.why: Each instance has its own /tmp, in memory; files go missing.

choices.text: To a managed instance group that replaces machines
choices.why: A replaced machine comes back without the files.

choices.text: To GKE Autopilot, as a Deployment
choices.why: A rescheduled pod loses what it wrote locally.

prompt: By lesson 23, what makes the Functions Framework a seam rather than a tie?
hint: It ran on a laptop with no network.

choices.text: Google promises never to change it
choices.why: No such promise exists; the point is who else can run it.

choices.text: It translates functions into Knative YAML
choices.why: It serves functions over HTTP; it writes no YAML.

choices.text: It is billed separately from Cloud Run
choices.why: A function runs on Cloud Run and is billed as Cloud Run.

choices.text: It is open source and serves the same code anywhere Python runs
choices.why: Right. Nothing in the function itself says Google.

prompt: With lesson 23's tiers (first GiB free, 0.12 to 1 TiB, 0.11 to 10 TiB, 0.08 beyond), what do 3 TiB (3,072 GiB) of egress in one month cost, in USD?
hint: Lesson 23. 1,023 GiB at 0.12, then 2,048 at 0.11.

prompt: Match each dependency of the shop to what leaving it takes, as lesson 23's record says.
hint: Lesson 23.

pairs.left: Cloud Run for orders and web

pairs.right: Any scheduler that can call a URL
The months left on the term

prompt: A finance lead proposes a three-year commitment covering twice today's Cloud Run usage, "since we will grow". What does lesson 23 say?
hint: Lesson 23. Saved or promised?

choices.text: Agree: longer terms always give larger discounts
choices.why: The discount is real; the half that is not used yet is still paid.

choices.text: Commit to the baseline that already runs; the rest is money promised
choices.why: Right. A discount on capacity you hope to need is a bill for capacity you may not.

choices.text: Agree, as long as the commitment is resource-based
choices.why: The kind of commitment does not change paying for unused capacity.

choices.text: Refuse any commitment, since it is a kind of lock-in
choices.why: Lock-in chosen for a price worth paying is the lesson's point.

prompt: Lesson 23 calls a place where your system meets the provider through an interface somebody else also implements a ___.
hint: A word from tailoring.

prompt: A team's instance template boots from the family shop-web. On Tuesday a bad build is published, and by Wednesday half the group runs it. What is the quickest way to stop new machines getting it?
hint: Lesson 2. What does a family read?

choices.text: Delete the family, so the template falls back to Debian
choices.why: A family is a label on images, not an object with a fallback.

choices.text: Edit the template to name an older family
choices.why: Templates cannot be edited; a new template is slower than one deprecation.

choices.text: Deprecate the bad build
choices.why: Right. The family points back to the previous image at once.

choices.text: Mark the bad build DELETED, which removes it from storage at once
choices.why: DELETED is a label; the image stays until somebody deletes it.

prompt: A g2-standard-4 costs 0.706832276 USD an hour. A team runs it 9 hours on each of 22 working days instead of all month. What does it cost that month, to the cent?
hint: Lesson 2. 198 hours.

prompt: A plan reads data "google_compute_image" and hangs for minutes on the train with no network. What is happening?
hint: Lesson 2. When is a data source read?

choices.text: It retries the API its data source needs
choices.why: Right. The lesson's run took five and a half minutes to fail.

choices.text: Terraform is downloading the Debian image to the laptop
choices.why: Nothing is downloaded; it asks a question.

choices.text: The provider is waiting for the token no-account to expire
choices.why: The token is never checked without a network.

choices.text: Packer is building the image the data source names
choices.why: Packer is a separate tool, run separately.

prompt: A machine with a GPU stops for host maintenance instead of migrating, so it is written with on_host_maintenance = "___".
hint: Lesson 2. The other value is MIGRATE.

prompt: A single-machine PostgreSQL with no replica must survive the loss of a zone without restoring from backup. Which disk does lesson 3 point to?
hint: Lesson 3. Two zones, written synchronously.

choices.text: A local SSD, for speed
choices.why: It is lost with the host, never mind the zone.

choices.text: A pd-ssd with nightly snapshots
choices.why: Snapshots are a restore, which the question rules out.

choices.text: A Hyperdisk Balanced with more IOPS
choices.why: IOPS buys speed, not a second zone.

choices.text: A regional disk
choices.why: Right. A machine in the other zone attaches the replica and carries on.

prompt: A 500 GiB Hyperdisk Balanced is provisioned at 4,000 IOPS and 240 MBps. With 0.08 per GiB-month, 0.005 per IOPS-month above 3,000 and 0.04 per MBps-month above 140, what is a month, in USD?
hint: Lesson 3. 40 + 5 + 4.

prompt: A batch machine keeps its working files on a local SSD and is stopped every evening by a script to save money. What does the team find each morning?
hint: Lesson 3. Stopping moves the machine off its host.

choices.text: The files, as after a reboot
choices.why: A reboot keeps them; a stop does not unless preserved.

choices.text: An empty local SSD, unless preservation was asked for
choices.why: Right. Write state somewhere durable before the stop.

choices.text: A bill that stopped charging for the SSD overnight
choices.why: Saving money is the motive, not the surprise.

choices.text: A snapshot of the SSD taken at the stop
choices.why: Local SSDs have no snapshots.

prompt: Which of these are true of snapshots taken by a schedule? Choose all that apply.
hint: Lesson 3.

choices.text: Each one after the first holds only changed blocks
choices.why: Right; they are incremental.

choices.text: Deleting the oldest leaves the newer ones restorable
choices.why: Right; needed blocks are moved forward.

choices.text: start_time is read in São Paulo time
choices.why: It is UTC.

choices.text: A restore writes back over the original disk
choices.why: A restore makes a new disk.

prompt: The plan refused KEEP_SNAPSHOTS because on_source_disk_delete only accepts APPLY_RETENTION_POLICY or KEEP_AUTO____.
hint: Lesson 3. The word that keeps them after the disk is gone.

prompt: terraform apply fails with "resource is in use" while deleting an old instance template after a change. Which line was missing?
hint: Lesson 4. Which order works?

choices.text: name_prefix, so the template gets a fresh name
choices.why: A name clash fails at creation, not at deletion.

choices.text: target_size in the group
choices.why: The size has nothing to do with templates being deleted.

choices.text: create_before_destroy in the lifecycle block
choices.why: Right. Without it Terraform deletes the template the group still uses first.

choices.text: max_unavailable_fixed = 0 in the update policy
choices.why: The policy replaces machines; it does not order template deletion.

prompt: A regional group across three zones has target_size = 8, spread as evenly as the group allows. How is it spread?
hint: Lesson 4. Zones differ by at most one.

choices.text: Three, three and two
choices.why: Right. No two zones differ by more than one.

choices.text: Four, four and none
choices.why: That leaves a zone empty, the opposite of a regional group.

choices.text: Eight in the first zone listed
choices.why: That is a zonal group.

choices.text: Four, two and two, the first zone taking the remainder twice
choices.why: Four against two breaks the rule of one.

prompt: A new template has a broken health endpoint. Which update setting limits the damage to one machine of three?
hint: Lesson 4. One machine first.

choices.text: type = "OPPORTUNISTIC" on the update policy
choices.why: It still spreads the template as machines are recreated.

choices.text: max_surge_fixed = 3
choices.why: Surge adds capacity; it does not hold the new template back.

choices.text: initial_delay_sec raised to 600
choices.why: A longer delay only postpones the failures.

choices.text: A canary version with target_size fixed = 1
choices.why: Right. Two machines stay on the stable template.

prompt: Match each symptom to the setting the lessons on groups say to look at.
hint: Lesson 4.

pairs.left: New machines are deleted before they finish booting
Every machine fails its check and the service is fine
An update briefly leaves only two machines serving
A machine deleted by hand comes back

prompt: A team puts its single orders database in a regional managed group "for resilience". What goes wrong first?
hint: Lesson 4. What does a replacement start from?

choices.text: The group refuses machines with a data disk
choices.why: Nothing refuses it; the trouble comes later.

choices.text: A replacement or rebalancing starts from the template, without the data
choices.why: Right. Stateful MIGs exist, and they are the last resort.

choices.text: The database runs three copies that disagree
choices.why: That needs target_size above one; the first problem is losing data.

choices.text: The health check cannot reach port 5432
choices.why: Any port can be checked.

prompt: Six machines run at 50% CPU with a target of 0.75, so the autoscaler recommends ___ machines.
hint: Lesson 5. 3 machines of work.

prompt: An order-confirmation worker reads from a queue; on sale days the backlog grows to thousands while its CPU stays at 25%. Which change fixes the scaling?
hint: Lesson 5. Measure the work waiting.

choices.text: Lower the CPU target to 0.2
choices.why: It helps a little and still follows the wrong signal.

choices.text: Add a schedule for sale days
choices.why: A schedule guesses; the queue measures.

choices.text: Scale on undelivered messages per machine
choices.why: Right. It grows before anybody waits.

choices.text: Turn on predictive autoscaling
choices.why: Prediction learns the CPU pattern, which is not the problem.

prompt: A group peaks at 10 machines; the load then needs 4, and scale-in control allows 2 every 10 minutes. Order the sizes the group passes through.
hint: Lesson 5.
trap: It takes thirty minutes to reach 4, and the machines are still there if the load comes back.

prompt: A schedule says min_required_replicas = 8 from nine to six; at noon the CPU rule wants 11. How many machines run?
hint: Lesson 5. A floor, not a size.

choices.why: Right. The floor is 8 and CPU asks for more.

choices.text: 8, since the schedule overrides the CPU rule
choices.why: A schedule only raises the minimum.

choices.text: 19, the sum of both
choices.why: The autoscaler takes the larger, not the sum.

choices.text: The max_replicas value, during a schedule
choices.why: Schedules do not jump to the ceiling.

prompt: A report job on Spot writes its results only at the end, after five hours. What change makes it a good Spot tenant?
hint: Lesson 6. What does a preemption cost it now?

choices.text: A longer shutdown script that uploads partial results
choices.why: The thirty seconds do not stretch for a long script.

choices.text: max_run_duration of six hours
choices.why: A time limit stops runaways; it saves no progress.

choices.text: instance_termination_action = "STOP"
choices.why: STOP keeps the disk, not the work in memory.

choices.text: Splitting the work and saving each piece as it finishes
choices.why: Right. A preemption then costs one piece.

prompt: Ten c4a-standard-2 machines run 730 hours on Spot at 0.044388 USD an hour instead of 0.0898 on demand. What is saved in the month, to the cent?
hint: Lesson 6. The hourly difference, times 730, times ten.

prompt: A service run by systemd on a Spot machine has no SIGTERM handler. What happens to the request it is serving at preemption?
hint: Lesson 6. Exit code 143.

choices.text: It finishes, because Compute Engine waits thirty seconds
choices.why: The wait helps only a program that handles the signal.

choices.text: It is cut off: the process dies when the signal arrives
choices.why: Right. The thirty seconds were there and nothing used them.

choices.text: It is moved to another machine by live migration
choices.why: Spot machines are preempted, not migrated.

choices.text: systemd ignores SIGTERM for services by default
choices.why: systemd sends it; the default action is to die.

prompt: Which belong on Spot by lesson 6's test? Choose all that apply.
hint: Lesson 6. Would anyone need to act?

choices.text: Pull-request test runners
choices.why: Right; a run is retried.

choices.text: The only Redis holding shopping carts
choices.why: It holds state nobody can rebuild.

choices.text: Extra web machines behind a standard base
choices.why: Right; the base answers if they go.

choices.text: Every web machine, to save 40%
choices.why: A shortage would take them all at once.

prompt: A startup script appends a line to /etc/hosts and installs a package with no condition. The machine is restarted twice for patches. What state is it in?
hint: Lesson 7. When does the guest environment run the script?

choices.text: As after the first boot: scripts run once, at creation
choices.why: The script runs on every boot, not once.

choices.text: Recreated by Terraform, since metadata changed
choices.why: A restart changes no metadata, and Terraform was not run.

choices.text: The line three times over
choices.why: Right. A script that runs on every boot has to be safe to repeat.

choices.text: Stopped, because a startup script that changes /etc fails the boot
choices.why: A script never stops the boot, failing or not.

prompt: A PDF service on a VM follows links found in uploaded documents. A document links to http://metadata.google.internal/computeMetadata/v1/instance/service-accounts/default/token. What protects the token, and what limits the damage if that fails?
hint: Lesson 7. A filter, and what the token is worth.

choices.text: The header rule, then a narrow account
choices.why: Right. A forged fetch rarely sets the header, and a dedicated account limits the rest.

choices.text: The private address: only the VM's own network reaches it
choices.why: The fetch is made from the VM, which reaches it fine.

choices.text: The token's one-hour life, which makes it useless to steal
choices.why: An hour is plenty to use a stolen token.

choices.text: OS Login, which blocks reads by non-human users
choices.why: OS Login governs SSH, not the metadata server.

prompt: A machine's calls to Pub/Sub fail with a permission error although the account holds roles/pubsub.publisher on the topic. Which could explain it? Choose all that apply.
hint: Lesson 7. Two checks, and which identity is calling.

choices.text: The instance was created with only the storage-ro scope
choices.why: Right; the token cannot call Pub/Sub at all.

choices.text: No service_account block, so the default account is calling
choices.why: Right; the role is on a different identity.

choices.text: The metadata server only issues tokens for Cloud Storage
choices.why: It issues tokens for whatever the scopes cover.

choices.text: GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS points at another account's key file
choices.why: Right; that file comes first in the search order.

prompt: Code that calls google.auth.default() is tested on a laptop with gcloud's application-default login and then deployed to a VM with an attached account. What changes in the code?
hint: Lesson 7. The same search order everywhere.

choices.text: A key file must be copied so the VM finds credentials
choices.why: That is exactly what the attached account avoids.

choices.text: The project must be passed explicitly on a VM
choices.why: The metadata server knows the project.

choices.text: GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS must be set to the metadata address
choices.why: That variable names a file, and setting it would stop the search there.

choices.text: Nothing; on the VM the metadata server answers
choices.why: Right. That is what the order is for.

prompt: A Node.js image runs fine with docker run -p 3000:3000 on a laptop but its Cloud Run deployment fails, saying the container did not listen on the port in PORT. The server code calls listen(3000). What is the fix?
hint: Lesson 8. Who chooses the port?

choices.text: Publish port 3000 in the Dockerfile with EXPOSE
choices.why: EXPOSE documents a port; Cloud Run still probes PORT.

choices.text: Listen on process.env.PORT, on every interface
choices.why: Right. Cloud Run sends requests to PORT, 8080 by default.

choices.text: Raise the startup probe's timeout
choices.why: Waiting longer on the wrong port never succeeds.

choices.text: Rebuild the image for linux/amd64
choices.why: An architecture problem stops the start, not the listening.

prompt: A service with the shell-form CMD is scaled in four times a day for 30 days. Each scale-in waits the full grace period before SIGKILL, as the shell-form container did at home. How many minutes of waiting is that in a month?
hint: Lesson 8. Ten seconds each time.

prompt: A service caches product prices in a Python dictionary filled on the first request. After a deployment, some users see new prices and others old ones for a while. Why?
hint: Lesson 8. How many copies hold the dictionary?

choices.text: Cloud Run serves cached responses from its front end
choices.why: The front end does not cache responses.

choices.text: The dictionary is written to /tmp and shared slowly
choices.why: Nothing is shared between instances.

choices.text: Each instance filled its own cache, at its own moment
choices.why: Right. Memory is per instance, and instances come and go.

choices.text: Python dictionaries are not safe to read concurrently
choices.why: Reads are not the problem; the copies are.

prompt: Match each observation at home to what it predicts on Cloud Run.
hint: Lesson 8. The laptop is the cheapest place to find out.

pairs.left: docker stop takes ten seconds, exit 137
pairs.right: Requests in flight are cut on scale-in
The service works whatever PORT says

pairs.left: Logs print one JSON object per line

right_distractors: The image is too large to deploy

prompt: A new revision fails one request in a thousand. The service takes 2,000 requests an hour and the canary gets 5%. Roughly how long until the error has shown up ten times?
hint: Lesson 9. 10,000 requests at 100 an hour.

choices.text: About a hundred hours, four days
choices.why: Right. A small share of little traffic sees little.

choices.text: About ten hours
choices.why: That would be at 50%.

choices.text: About fifty hours
choices.why: That would be at 10%.

choices.text: About an hour, since 2,000 is more than a thousand
choices.why: Only 5% of the 2,000 reach the canary.

prompt: Terraform sets the split 80/20 between orders-v1 and orders-v2. Someone runs gcloud run services update-traffic to roll back to orders-v1 at 100. What does the next terraform plan show?
hint: Lesson 9. Who owns the traffic list?

choices.text: No changes, since the rollback created no revision
choices.why: Traffic is part of the service Terraform describes.

choices.text: An error, because gcloud locked the service
choices.why: Nothing is locked.

choices.text: A new revision orders-v3 to be created
choices.why: The template did not change.

choices.text: A change putting 20% back on orders-v2
choices.why: Right. Write the rollback into the file too, or the next apply undoes it.

prompt: A release of orders-v3 needs a database column added before it starts using it. Put the safe order.
hint: Lesson 9. Keep the way back open.
items: Add the column, which the old code ignores
Deploy orders-v3 with --no-traffic and test its tag
Move traffic to it in stages
Remove anything only the old code needed, once nobody will roll back
trap: Removing what the old code needs before the rollout ends makes the rollback fail on data.

prompt: A team wants every deployment to go live immediately except during the Black Friday week, when they want canaries. Which traffic setup fits?
hint: Lesson 9. LATEST moves; named revisions stay.

choices.text: A permanent split with a canary tag at 0%
choices.why: A tag alone never moves user traffic.

choices.text: LATEST at 100% normally; that week, --no-traffic and staged moves
choices.why: Right, and --to-latest afterwards, or later deploys stay dark.

choices.text: Named revisions always, with --to-latest after each deploy
choices.why: That works, but it is a manual step every time.

choices.text: min_instance_count on the new revision
choices.why: That keeps instances warm; it does not split traffic.

prompt: A nightly job resizes 30,000 photos, each picked by id % CLOUD_RUN_TASK_COUNT. Someone raises --tasks from 10 to 12 while an execution is being retried. What can happen?
hint: Lesson 10. What does changing the count do to a hash cut?

choices.text: Nothing: each task re-reads the count at the start
choices.why: Re-reading a new count is exactly what moves the assignments.

choices.text: Cloud Run refuses to change a job with a running execution
choices.why: The lesson makes no such promise; the risk is in the cut.

choices.text: Assignments shift, so some photos are done twice and others missed
choices.why: Right, unless the work is idempotent and the run starts fresh.

choices.text: The two new tasks wait for the next night
choices.why: Tasks belong to an execution, not to a night.

prompt: A job has --tasks=60, --parallelism=12, tasks of about 5 minutes and no failures. About how many minutes does the execution take?
hint: Lesson 10. Rounds times the length of one.

prompt: A job's program catches every exception, logs it as ERROR and exits normally. A task fails to reach the database. What does Cloud Run record?
hint: Lesson 10. What is the verdict made of?

choices.text: A success: the exit status was 0
choices.why: Right. A job that fails must exit non-zero, or nothing retries or alerts.

choices.text: A failed task, from the ERROR line
choices.why: Logs are not read for the verdict.

choices.text: A retry, since the database was unreachable
choices.why: Cloud Run cannot see the database; it sees the exit.

choices.text: A timeout, because the task never finished its work
choices.why: It finished quickly, by exiting.

prompt: To start a job at 06:00 in São Paulo, a Cloud Scheduler job needs schedule "0 6 * * *" and time_zone America/___.
hint: Lesson 10. An IANA zone name.

prompt: A service spends 300 ms per request waiting on another API and 5 ms computing. It runs with concurrency 1 and a burst of 200 simultaneous requests starts 200 instances. What does the lesson suggest first?
hint: Lesson 11. Waiting is what threads share.

choices.text: A minimum of 200 instances, so none start cold
choices.why: That pays for 200 idle instances all month.

choices.text: Instance-based billing, since it is cheaper per second
choices.why: Billing does not change how many instances start.

choices.text: Startup CPU boost, to start the 200 faster
choices.why: Faster starts of instances that need not exist.

choices.text: Measure what one instance carries and raise the concurrency
choices.why: Right. A waiting service can share an instance among many requests.

prompt: Using lesson 11's rates (active 0.000024 per vCPU-second and 0.0000025 per GiB-second; instance-based 0.000018 and 0.000002), at what busy share, in per cent, do the two billings cost the same for 1 vCPU and 0.5 GiB? Answer to the nearest per cent.
hint: Lesson 11. 0.000019 divided by 0.00002525.

prompt: A service loads a 400 MB machine-learning model at start-up, before it listens. Its first request after a quiet hour takes eight seconds. Which change attacks the cause rather than hiding it?
hint: Lesson 11. Your part of the cold start.

choices.text: min_instance_count = 1
choices.why: That hides the start; the cause stays.

choices.text: Load less before listening, or load the model on first use
choices.why: Right. What the program does before it listens is yours to shorten.

choices.text: A larger max_instance_count
choices.why: More instances means more cold starts, not shorter ones.

choices.text: Concurrency raised to 1,000
choices.why: Concurrency does not shorten a start.

prompt: A service that answers and then keeps working in a background thread loses its CPU under the default allocation; that work belongs in a ___ or a job.
hint: Lesson 11. Lesson 20 has one called Cloud Tasks.

prompt: Load testing at home shows a median of 0.2 s and a slowest request of 2 s at 80 concurrent requests, but steady times at 20. What should the Cloud Run concurrency be set to, by the lesson's reasoning?
hint: Lesson 11. Where the slowest pulls away from the median.

choices.text: 80, since the median stayed at 0.2 s
choices.why: The slowest requests are the users who complain.

choices.text: 1, to be safe
choices.why: Twenty were steady; one wastes instances.

choices.text: Around 20, where it stayed steady
choices.why: Right. The setting is a ceiling; the program decides what it carries.

choices.text: 1,000, so one instance takes every burst
choices.why: It already struggled at 80.

prompt: A new Cloud Run service must reach a Memorystore cache at 10.30.0.4, and the network team offers an empty /24 subnet for it. Which arrangement fits best?
hint: Lesson 12. Nothing extra to run, nothing extra on the bill.

choices.text: Direct VPC egress into the /24, with PRIVATE_RANGES_ONLY
choices.why: Right. Room for addresses, no machines in between.

choices.text: A connector with min_instances 2, so the cache has a fixed source range
choices.why: Nothing here asks for a fixed range, and the connector bills its machines all month.

choices.text: ALL_TRAFFIC with Cloud NAT, so the cache sees one address
choices.why: NAT is for the internet; a private address is reached without it.

choices.text: INGRESS_TRAFFIC_INTERNAL_ONLY on the service
choices.why: Ingress governs who calls the service, not where it connects.

prompt: A connector keeps min_instances = 3 of e2-micro, at 6.11 USD a month each on the price sheet. What is its floor for a year, in USD?
hint: Lesson 12. Three machines, twelve months.

prompt: A team locks a reporting service to INGRESS_TRAFFIC_INTERNAL_ONLY. A caller inside another Cloud Run service with no VPC access now fails. Which change fixes it without opening the service to the internet?
hint: Lesson 12. How does a call count as internal?

choices.text: Grant the caller roles/run.invoker on the reporting service
choices.why: The network check refuses before identity is looked at.

choices.text: Switch the reporting service's egress to ALL_TRAFFIC
choices.why: Egress never changes who may call in.

choices.text: Set the reporting service to INGRESS_TRAFFIC_ALL
choices.why: That is the opening the question rules out.

choices.text: Give the caller direct VPC egress
choices.why: Right. Its calls then leave through the VPC and count as internal.

prompt: Which of these would a clean terraform plan of a Cloud Run service with vpc_access NOT have checked? Choose all that apply.
hint: Lesson 12. The plan reads your files on your laptop.

choices.text: That the subnet named exists in the region
choices.why: Right; Cloud Run checks it when the revision is created.

choices.text: That egress is one of the accepted values
choices.why: The provider refuses an unknown value at validate.

choices.text: That a connector given by reference does not clash with network_interfaces
choices.why: Right; the reference is unknown until apply.

choices.text: That ingress is spelled as the provider expects
choices.why: An unknown ingress value is refused at validate.

prompt: A regional pool covering three zones has node_count = 2 of e2-standard-4, at 97.84 USD a month each. What do its nodes cost a month at that size, in USD?
hint: Lesson 13. The count is per zone.

prompt: A payments team wants node upgrades that keep every old node until the new ones have run cleanly for a while, and can be rolled back. Which upgrade setting fits, and at what price?
hint: Lesson 13. One strategy keeps a soak period.

choices.text: SURGE with max_surge 1 and max_unavailable 0, at one extra node
choices.why: Surge replaces old nodes as it goes; nothing waits to roll back to.

choices.text: BLUE_GREEN, doubling the pool's machines during the upgrade
choices.why: Right. The old set stays through the soak period.

choices.text: The STABLE channel, which upgrades nodes only after a soak
choices.why: A channel picks versions; how nodes are replaced is the pool's setting.

choices.text: A NO_UPGRADES exclusion renewed every month
choices.why: That postpones upgrades; it gives no rollback.

prompt: A team in São Paulo wants maintenance between 01:00 and 07:00 local time on weekends. What start_time of day should the recurring window carry?
hint: Lesson 13. The times are UTC, and São Paulo is three hours behind.

choices.text: 01:00 UTC, since GKE converts to the cluster's region
choices.why: Nothing converts; 01:00 UTC is 22:00 the evening before.
That is subtracting three hours instead of adding them.
Right. 01:00 in São Paulo is 04:00 UTC.
That would start the window at 04:00 local.

prompt: A cluster on no release channel has its channel set to ___, and GKE upgrades it anyway once its version leaves support.
hint: Lesson 13. One of the five values the provider listed.

prompt: On Autopilot at 0.0445 USD per vCPU-hour and 0.0049225 per GiB-hour, what do four pods requesting 0.5 vCPU and 2 GiB each cost for 730 hours, in USD?
hint: Lesson 14. Sum the requests first.

prompt: A batch platform runs forty identical pods of 1 vCPU and 4 GiB around the clock, with nothing privileged. Which mode does the lesson's arithmetic favour, and why?
hint: Lesson 14. When do nodes sit partly empty?

choices.text: Standard: steady pods fill nodes, and a node costs less per vCPU
choices.why: Right; the same pattern as the twelve big pods.

choices.text: Autopilot, because nothing is privileged
choices.why: That only says Autopilot is allowed, not that it is cheaper.

choices.text: Autopilot, because Standard always pays an extra cluster fee
choices.why: Both pay the same fee.

choices.text: Standard, because Autopilot refuses more than thirty pods
choices.why: There is no such limit in the lesson.

prompt: A security agent ships as a privileged DaemonSet with hostPath mounts. On an Autopilot cluster, when does it fail?
hint: Lesson 14. Who refuses pods?

choices.text: At terraform validate, as a conflict with enable_autopilot
choices.why: The DaemonSet is not in the Terraform files.

choices.text: Never: DaemonSets are exempt from Autopilot's rules
choices.why: DaemonSets are allowed, not exempt.

choices.text: Only when Google next upgrades the nodes
choices.why: The refusal comes at creation.

choices.text: At pod creation, by admission controls
choices.why: Right; nothing in Terraform sees a pod.

prompt: A team moving to Autopilot asks what it still decides itself. Choose all that apply.
hint: Lesson 14. Pods, not nodes.

choices.text: The CPU and memory each container requests
choices.why: Right; on Autopilot the request is the bill.

choices.text: The machine type of the nodes
choices.why: Google picks it from the requests.

choices.text: Whether a pod asks for Spot capacity
choices.why: Right, with a node selector.

choices.text: The surge settings of node upgrades
choices.why: There is no node pool to set them on.

prompt: A team ran its Standard cluster for a year and now wants Autopilot. What does the move involve?
hint: Lesson 14. The mode is fixed at creation.

choices.text: Setting enable_autopilot = true and one terraform apply
choices.why: The mode cannot change on an existing cluster.

choices.text: A new cluster and a redeploy
choices.why: Right, minus anything Autopilot refuses; the cost is the migration, not a rewrite.

choices.text: Rewriting every Deployment for Autopilot's API
choices.why: The objects mostly move unchanged.

choices.text: Deleting the node pools so the cluster converts itself
choices.why: Nothing converts a cluster.

prompt: A pod in the namespace billing, running as the Kubernetes service account invoices, must read a bucket through the Google service account invoice-reader. Which member goes on the workloadIdentityUser binding?
hint: Lesson 15. Pool, then [namespace/name].

choices.text: serviceAccount:invoice-reader@planner-dev.iam.gserviceaccount.com
choices.why: That is the account being acted as, not who acts.

choices.text: serviceAccount:planner-dev.svc.id.goog[invoices/billing]
choices.why: Reversed: IAM would see a different identity and say nothing.

choices.text: serviceAccount:planner-dev.svc.id.goog[billing/invoices]
choices.why: Right; namespace first, then the Kubernetes service account.

choices.text: planner-dev.svc.id.goog[billing/invoices]
choices.why: The member needs its kind in front; validate refuses it.

prompt: A key file for a service account appears in a public repository. Under Workload Identity, what is the equivalent risk?
hint: Lesson 15. What exists that could leak?

choices.text: None of the same kind: only tokens that expire within about an hour
choices.why: Right; there is no long-lived secret to leak.

choices.text: The workload pool name, which grants access to anyone who knows it
choices.why: A pool name is an identifier, not a credential.

choices.text: The annotation on the Kubernetes service account
choices.why: It names an email; it proves nothing by itself.

choices.text: The base64 Secret GKE creates for each pod
choices.why: GKE creates no such Secret.

prompt: Order the steps of replacing a static key with Workload Identity for an existing pod, safest first.
hint: Lesson 15. The key goes only when nothing needs it.
items: Enable the workload pool and GKE_METADATA on the nodes
Grant the binding and annotate the Kubernetes service account
Redeploy the pod without the mounted key and confirm it reads the bucket
Delete the key at Google and the Secret in the cluster
trap: Deleting the key first breaks the pod before its replacement identity works.

prompt: Match each Workload Identity setup to what it needs.
hint: Lesson 15. Two ways, and the node setting under both.

pairs.left: Acting as a Google service account
pairs.right: A workloadIdentityUser binding and an annotation
A principal:// member with the project number

pairs.left: Pods on a Standard node pool

right_distractors: A JSON key mounted from a Secret

prompt: A game server in GKE speaks UDP to players on the internet. What should expose it?
hint: Lesson 16. Which load balancer is not about HTTP?

choices.text: An Ingress with a ManagedCertificate
choices.why: An Ingress routes HTTP; it cannot carry a game's UDP.

choices.text: A Gateway of class gke-l7-global-external-managed
choices.why: That class is a layer-7 HTTP load balancer.

choices.text: A NEG annotation on a ClusterIP Service
choices.why: A NEG is a backend for a load balancer, not one itself.

choices.text: A Service of type LoadBalancer
choices.why: Right; a passthrough load balancer forwards it untouched.

prompt: Right after a rollout, a team with node backends sees errors for a minute while Kubernetes reports every new pod ready. What would container-native load balancing change?
hint: Lesson 16. When does a new pod count as ready?

choices.text: Nothing: the minute is the load balancer's fixed delay
choices.why: The gap comes from readiness not reaching the load balancer.

choices.text: Ready would wait for the load balancer
choices.why: Right; with the readiness gate a pod is ready only once healthy in the load balancer.

choices.text: Requests would be mirrored to old and new pods
choices.why: Nothing mirrors requests.

choices.text: The load balancer would move to the pods' zone
choices.why: Its location is not the issue.

prompt: An HTTPRoute sends weight 95 to orders and 5 to orders-next. Out of 40,000 requests, about how many reach orders-next?
hint: Lesson 16. Five parts in a hundred.

prompt: In the Gateway API, the object that says which kind of load balancer to build, and which GKE provides, is the Gateway___.
hint: Lesson 16. Owned by Google, not by a team.

prompt: A function that resizes uploads opens a database connection inside the handler on every call, and under load the database runs out of connections. What is the change lesson 17 points to?
hint: Lesson 17. What is safe to share between calls on one instance?

choices.text: Raise max_instance_count so each call gets its own instance
choices.why: More instances open more connections, not fewer.

choices.text: Store the connection in a global counter keyed by request
choices.why: A per-request key still opens one per call.

choices.text: Open it once at module level and reuse it
choices.why: Right. Expensive, shareable work goes outside the function, like PRICES.

choices.text: Move the function to the first generation, one request per instance
choices.why: That multiplies instances, and with them connections.

prompt: A CloudEvent sent to a function carries ce-id, ce-type and ce-source but its sender forgot ce-specversion. What does the function's own code see?
hint: Lesson 17. The framework reads the attributes first.

choices.text: Nothing: the framework answers 400 before calling it
choices.why: Right. A required attribute missing means no CloudEvent and no call.

choices.text: An event whose specversion defaults to 1.0
choices.why: Nothing is filled in; a missing attribute makes it no CloudEvent.

choices.text: The raw HTTP request, since parsing failed
choices.why: The function is not called with a fallback.

choices.text: An event with an empty specversion string
choices.why: The framework refuses rather than passing it on.

prompt: With the quote function's prices (mug 3500, tee 7900, poster 2500 cents), what total_cents does an order of two tees and four posters return?
Match each piece of work to the shape lessons 17 and 18 would give it.
hint: Lessons 17 and 18. Who calls, and is anyone waiting?

pairs.left: A price quote the checkout waits for
A thumbnail for each uploaded photo
An inventory entry for each new VM in the project
Reacting to every order published by the web service

right_distractors: A Compute Engine machine polling every minute

prompt: A trigger function charges a card and has retries turned on. The payment provider confirms the charge, but the function crashes before returning. What happens next, and what prevents a double charge?
hint: Lesson 18. At least once.

choices.text: Nothing, because a crash after the work counts as success
choices.why: No 2xx came back, so the event is delivered again.

choices.text: The event moves straight to the dead-letter topic
choices.why: Only after the last allowed attempt.

choices.text: It is delivered again, and turning retries off afterwards undoes the charge
choices.why: Nothing undoes a charge already made.

choices.text: It returns; handled event ids stop the repeat
choices.why: Right. Idempotence by event id is the first defence.

prompt: The emulator redelivered a failing message about once a second: 10 deliveries in the 10 seconds the lab waited. At that pace, how many deliveries would one minute of failure produce?
hint: Lesson 18. Ten in ten seconds.

prompt: A team moves the thumbnails function from a Cloud Storage Pub/Sub notification to an Eventarc storage trigger, and every event now fails with a KeyError on "message". Why?
hint: Lesson 18. The envelope differs.

choices.text: Eventarc delivers storage events as pull messages
choices.why: It pushes a CloudEvent like every other source.

choices.text: The data is the object JSON, with no message
choices.why: Right. The metadata is the same; the parsing must change.

choices.text: The bucket attribute must be named bucketId in the trigger
choices.why: The criterion is bucket; the error is in the parsing.

choices.text: Storage events need audit logs enabled first
choices.why: Storage events are direct.

prompt: Someone wants a function to run whenever a Cloud Storage object is read, and builds an audit-log trigger on storage.objects.get. Nothing ever fires. What is the most likely reason?
hint: Lesson 18. Two kinds of audit log.

choices.text: Reads are delivered only to pull subscriptions
choices.why: Delivery does not depend on the method.

choices.text: The trigger must name the object, not the bucket
choices.why: Naming is not what stops it.

choices.text: Data access logs are off, so reads write no audit entry
choices.why: Right. An unlogged method never fires, and nothing says so.

choices.text: Audit-log triggers deliver only after 24 hours
choices.why: They take minutes, not a day.

prompt: An App Engine standard service set to F1 is visited by staff from 9:00 to 17:00 and scales to zero otherwise, one instance while open. What does it cost per day?
hint: Lesson 19. Compare the hours with the daily allowance.

choices.text: Nothing; 8 hours fit in the 28 free
choices.why: Right. The free F hours are per day per project.

choices.text: 0.40 USD: 8 hours at 0.05
choices.why: The daily free allowance comes first.

choices.text: 1.20 USD: a full day of 24 hours at 0.05
choices.why: It scales to zero outside opening hours.

choices.text: 43.58 USD a month, the flexible price
choices.why: That is a flexible instance, which never scales to zero.

prompt: A flexible service runs its default two instances of 2 vCPU and 2 GiB all month. At 0.0526 per vCPU-hour and 0.0071 per GiB-hour, what does it cost for 730 hours, in USD?
A company acquires a startup whose App Engine app lives in us-central and must now serve Brazilian law from São Paulo. What does lesson 19 say the move takes?
hint: Lesson 19. The region is chosen once.

choices.text: Editing location_id and applying
choices.why: The application's region cannot change.

choices.text: Deploying a new version with a region setting
choices.why: Versions do not choose regions.

choices.text: Splitting traffic 50/50 between the two regions
choices.why: A split is between versions of one application.

choices.text: A new project and a migration
choices.why: Right. One application per project, one region forever.

prompt: To keep each visitor on one version during a 90/10 rollout, App Engine splits traffic by ___.
hint: Lesson 19. IP, random, or the third one.

prompt: A reporting job must call a partner API that allows 2 requests a second, for 10,000 records after a sale. Which tool from lesson 20 carries that limit?
hint: Lesson 20. Which product owns "how fast"?

choices.text: Cloud Scheduler, firing every half second
choices.why: Scheduler has a clock, not a rate limit, and fires at most each minute.

choices.text: A Cloud Tasks queue with max_dispatches_per_second = 2
choices.why: Right. The queue absorbs the burst at the partner's rate.

choices.text: A Pub/Sub push subscription to the partner
choices.why: A push subscription has no dispatch-rate setting of its own.

choices.text: A function with max_instance_count = 2
choices.why: Two instances can still send many requests a second.

prompt: That queue holds the 10,000 records and dispatches 2 a second. How many seconds does it take to drain, at best?
hint: Lesson 20. Tasks divided by rate.

prompt: With min_backoff 5s, max_backoff 100s and max_doublings 2, order the waits of the first five retries as they occur.
hint: Lesson 20. Two doublings, then a step of 5 x 2^2.
trap: After the doublings the wait grows by a fixed 20 s, so 40 is followed by 60, not 80.

prompt: A Scheduler job is set to "0 2 * * *" with time_zone America/New_York to start a São Paulo backup at 03:00 local time. What goes wrong?
hint: Lesson 20. The zone's own rules are followed.

choices.text: Nothing: the region southamerica-east1 overrides the zone
choices.why: The region does not set the time zone.

choices.text: Scheduler refuses zones outside the job's region
choices.why: Any IANA zone is accepted.

choices.text: New York's DST shifts it an hour twice a year
choices.why: Right. Name the zone the time is meant in: America/Sao_Paulo.

choices.text: The job runs at 02:00 UTC instead
choices.why: With a zone named, UTC is not used.

prompt: A handler behind a Cloud Tasks queue receives a task for an order that was cancelled and deleted. Which responses follow lesson 20? Choose all that apply.
hint: Lesson 20. Will time fix it?

choices.text: Log that the order no longer exists
choices.why: Right; the reason must be visible.

choices.text: Answer with a 2xx so the queue stops
choices.why: Right; no retry will find the order.

choices.text: Answer 503 so it is retried later
choices.why: Every attempt would fail the same way.

choices.text: Let the dispatch deadline pass without answering
choices.why: That is a failure and is retried.

prompt: A Cloud Run service in São Paulo starts slowly on every cold start, and its images live in a us-central1 repository. What change does lesson 21 suggest?
hint: Lesson 21. The region is part of the host.

choices.text: Store them close to where they run
choices.why: Right. Pulls stay in the region: faster, and no transfer between regions.

choices.text: Make the repository virtual
choices.why: A virtual repository still pulls from where the images are.

choices.text: Turn on immutable tags
choices.why: Tags do not move bytes closer.

choices.text: Add a cleanup policy to keep fewer versions
choices.why: Fewer stored versions do not speed a pull.

prompt: A team deploys web@sha256:… to production. The next day someone pushes a broken build as web:latest. What happens to production?
hint: Lesson 21. A digest names bytes.

choices.text: It picks up the broken build at the next restart
choices.why: Only a deployment by tag would.

choices.text: The push is refused because production uses the image
choices.why: Without immutable tags, the push succeeds.

choices.text: The registry rewrites the digest to the new build
choices.why: A digest cannot point at other bytes.

choices.text: Nothing: it runs the digest it was given
choices.why: Right. Moving latest cannot touch a deployment by digest.

prompt: A repository holds 40.5 GiB of images. At 0.10 USD per GiB-month after the first 0.5 GiB, what does a month of storage cost?
hint: Lesson 21.

prompt: A repository mode that caches an upstream such as Docker Hub, fetching on the first pull, is called ___.
hint: Lesson 21. Standard, virtual, or this one.
